# SkillSync v0.1.0 — First Release

> Create a Skill once, manage it in one place, and make it available to
> every supported AI coding tool.

SkillSync is a local-first desktop app + CLI that gives you a single
control plane over **Agent Skills** (`SKILL.md` directories) across AI
coding tools — with a canonical store as the single source of truth.

## ✨ Highlights

- **One canonical store** (`~/.agents/skills` by default, configurable,
  can be a git repo) — skills stay portable and usable without SkillSync.
- **First-class tool adapters**: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and Gemini
  CLI, each owning its own paths, detection, symlink semantics and reload
  guidance. Adding a tool = one adapter module.
- **Adopt existing skills safely**: first-run import classifies everything
  by content fingerprint — unique / exact duplicates / conflicts. Nothing
  is imported without your confirmation, and nothing is ever overwritten
  silently.
- **One-way sync** from the store into your tools: symlinks where safe
  (tool-aware — e.g. Gemini CLI gets copies since it doesn't follow
  symlinks), with `--dry-run` previews and per-change reports.
- **Skill × Tool matrix**: enable/disable any skill for any tool.
  Disabling removes only the SkillSync-managed installation — unmanaged
  user data is never touched.
- **Conflict management**: directory-aware diff with line-level text
  diffs, and explicit resolutions — *Use canonical*, *Import target*,
  *Keep both*, *Ignore*. Every replacement is backed up first.
- **Optional auto-sync**: a debounced filesystem watcher refreshes
  managed copies as you edit the store (off by default; symlinked tools
  need no copying). Manual *Refresh* / *Sync Now* always works.
- **Doctor diagnostics** and structured operation logs
  (`~/.skillsync/logs/`, no skill contents, credential lines redacted).
- **Git machine-sync**: the store can be a git repository — explicit
  `status` / `pull --ff-only` / `commit` / `push`. Never automatic.

## 🔒 Safety invariants

- Unmanaged skills are **never** overwritten or deleted — detect →
  report → ask, with timestamped backups under `~/.skillsync/backups/`
  before any replacement.
- Skill scripts are **never executed** — scanning, syncing and validation
  only read bytes.
- All filesystem mutations validate canonicalized paths and re-verify
  ownership at execution time; writes are atomic (temp + rename).
- No database, no server, no accounts, no cloud — fully offline, and
  nothing requires SkillSync to keep running (plain directory symlinks).

## 🖥️ Desktop app

Tauri 2 + React: **Skills** page (search, status/tool filters, per-tool
matrix chips, read-only SKILL.md preview, open in Finder), **Tools** page
(detection, locations, integration toggles, per-tool sync), **Settings**
(canonical root, sync method, auto-sync, git, doctor).

## ⌨️ CLI

```bash
skillsync list | tools | scan | doctor      # discovery & diagnostics
skillsync import-plan / import-all          # adopt existing skills
skillsync import <path> [--dry-run]         # import one skill
skillsync sync --tool claude [--dry-run]    # canonical → tool
skillsync enable|disable <skill> --tool <t> # matrix toggles
skillsync conflicts | diff | resolve        # conflict management
skillsync git status|pull|commit|push       # machine sync
```

Every command supports `--json`; exit codes are script-friendly
(`0` ok, `1` error, `2` usage).

## 📦 Install (macOS, Apple Silicon)

1. Download `SkillSync-v0.1.0.zip` from this release and unzip.
2. Move `SkillSync.app` to `/Applications`.
3. Launch — first run shows an import plan for any skills already on
   your machine.

Build from source (macOS/Linux):

```bash
pnpm install && pnpm tauri build
```

## ✅ Compatibility

- Verified against real community skill collections (e.g.
  [ponytail](https://github.com/DietrichGebert/ponytail)): multi-line
  YAML block scalars, extra frontmatter keys (`argument-hint`,
  `metadata`), and tool-specific files all round-trip untouched.
- Codex compatibility: SkillSync links whole skill *directories* (Codex
  skips file-level `SKILL.md` symlinks).
- Packaged and tested on **macOS (Apple Silicon)**. Linux builds work
  with the standard Tauri prerequisites; Windows is supported by the
  code (symlink → copy fallback) but not yet packaged in CI.

## 🚧 Not in this release (by design)

Marketplace, profiles, remote/WSL environments, remote skill
installation, skill execution, and MCP/prompt/provider sync are
intentionally out of scope — see the roadmap in
[`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`](https://github.com/vicode117/skill-sync/blob/main/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md).
